# Bounded nonbasic primitive-seed discovery: completed at the authorized cap

Status: numerical discovery only, no improved seed found, no nonexistence theorem. The exact reversed-seed counterexample in Section3 is self-contained but unverified.

1. Model and calibration.
The code max4_primitive_pep.py minimizes the saturated intrinsic primitive energy
V_h=2 sum_i h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_i h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-s(s+1)||g_n||^2
with s=sum h. It keeps the full gradient Gram matrix G positive semidefinite, trace(G)=1, f_0=0, and every ordered smooth-convex sample inequality Q_ij<=0. Thus it tests the full intrinsic primitive condition, not a quadratic-only or Huber-only relaxation. It records all primal data, all nonnegative interpolation multipliers, the dual PSD slack, and residuals.

The runtime is isolated in workers/max4/.venv-pep. Installed versions: cvxpy1.9.3, clarabel0.11.1, numpy2.5.3, scipy1.18.1. Each solve used one thread, max_iter150, time_limit10 seconds, and requested gap/feasibility tolerances1e-9. No core or verifier code was changed.

Six initial evaluations included known primitive blocks [sqrt(2)], [3/2,3/2], exact DP length3 and length7, and the two orderings of (17/10,2,6/5). The known primitive objectives were between -2.3e-9 and -1.7e-10, consistent with their exact zero optimum. The forward seed returned a negative value and the reversed seed returned a negative value. These calibration signs match the symbolic witnesses, rather than being counted as new mathematical conclusions.

2. Scope and complete budget.
The experiment then ran two local continuous SLSQP probes, of lengths3 and7, with all steps independently variable and constrained only to be nonnegative and to have shifted sum 1.002 times the corresponding exact-DP shifted mass (evaluated in floating point for discovery). Neither symmetry nor a recursive grammar was imposed. The starting points were small nonsymmetric perturbations of the DP blocks. The outer objective was minus the minimum primitive energy; its sensitivity used the computed primal and dual solutions. This is a local, nonsmooth numerical search, not a global optimization proof.

Total evaluations:60, including six calibration/candidate evaluations,24 local evaluations at length3 and30 at length7. The persistent counter in max4_pep_budget.json blocks further calls. Accumulated measured solve/build time was1.890137771 seconds. There were50 solver statuses `optimal` and10 `optimal_inaccurate`; no inaccurate output was promoted to a certificate.

Best sampled minimum energy at length3 was about -0.03623216044 (evaluation28), with h approximately
(1.4184351724,2.0071236092,1.4145251974).
Best sampled minimum energy at length7 was about -0.06114950110 (evaluation59), with h approximately
(1.4221824349,2.0110133066,1.4173278397,3.4184527329,1.4143778864,2.0014068997,1.4144488473).
Both were negative by amounts far larger than the recorded numerical residuals, and no credible improved primitive certificate appeared. The search stopped at the exact authorized evaluation cap. It did not test all nonbasic seeds, other initializations, lengths4 or5, or other target gains.

Across all60 evaluations, the largest positive interpolation residual was6.85e-8 and the most negative computed dual slack eigenvalue was-6.54e-7 (including inaccurate outputs). At the two best local samples, interpolation residuals were below4.3e-11; their slack eigenvalue minima were about-7.46e-11 and-1.36e-8. All full data and solver statuses are in max4_pep_evaluations.jsonl; the two local summaries are in max4_pep_local_summary.json. No exact feasibility or infeasibility assertion is inferred from these floating-point residuals.

3. Exact reconstruction for the reversed rational seed.
The rank-one numerical witness for h=(6/5,2,17/10) suggested gradients proportional to (1,1,-1,7/10). This was reconstructed without solver tolerances as follows.
Define f(y)=y^2/2 for y<=1 and f(y)=y-1/2 for y>=1. Its derivative min(y,1) is continuous, monotone and1-Lipschitz, so f is convex and1-smooth, with minimizer0. Starting at y_0=11/5, the three steps give exactly
y_1=1, y_2=-1, y_3=7/10,
with gradients1,1,-1,7/10. At all four points Q_(i,star)=0. With s=49/10 and R=59/10, the intrinsic primitive energy is therefore
V_h=(11/5)^2-(59/10)^2(7/10)^2=-122169/10000<0.
Its trace-normalized value is -122169/34900, explaining the numerical value near-3.5005444. The exact function, not a numerical rank determination, proves the seed's failure.
This also yields a useful specific test for schedules (H,2,C), with H>=0 and1<=C<=2: the same function starting at H+1 gives endpoints1,-1,C-1, so any primitive certificate must satisfy
(H+C+3)(C-1)<=H+1.
This is an additional witness condition, not a complete characterization of such schedules.

4. What remains.
The experiment found no nonbasic saturated seed with a proved positive gain and hence supplied no asymptotic negative construction. It does not establish that all primitive or all GD schedules are basic. The next analytic upper-bound attempt must change the invariant, rather than enlarge this scan or claim that numerical failure settles the seed question. In particular, a start/end gradient potential can retain cross terms omitted by a scalar primitive capacity; its one-step and two-step identities should be derived before any recursive closure is asserted.

https://clarabel.org/stable/api_settings/

claim: The concrete terminal-descent operations cannot be bootstrapped by first creating penultimate flow at fixed h: a full stationary primal forces delta_(n-1)>=q/2+||g_n||^2/2, and any such certificate inflation costs more than the subsequent blend gains.
evidence:
# Why creating penultimate flow first does not solve the stationary case

Status: unverified failure analysis of a specific proposed extension. The valid transfer and descent identities remain intact.

Consider a full matching stationary tuple (h,q,lambda,G,f) with q>0, h_{n-1}>0, all primal interpolation inequalities, dual PSD, complementarity, and the stepsize stationarity equations. Put p=g_{n-1}, g=g_n, delta=f_{n-1}-||p||^2/2.

## 1. Last-step stationarity selects an orthogonal terminal pair

For the SAME legal primal G selected by the full stationary tuple, one has

    <p,g>=0.                                               (1)

Here is a proof that does not assume a C2 function or differentiability of W. Realize the legal finite data by a convex 1-smooth interpolating function. Change only the final step b by a small real u. Then x_n(u)=x_n-u p, g_n(u)=g_n+O(u), and

    f_n(u)=f_n-u<p,g>+o(u).

Let D be the derivative of the full certificate matrix with respect to b, holding q and lambda fixed. The old matrix annihilates the old vector realization by PSD complementarity. Therefore its evaluation on the changed gradient vectors is O(u^2), and the full polynomial identity gives

    sum lambda_ij Q_ij(u)
       =u[<D,G>-2<p,g>]+o(u).

The left side is nonpositive for both signs of u and vanishes at zero. Consequently <D,G>=2<p,g>. The full stationarity equation <D,G>=0 proves (1). This argument keeps the same G; it does not substitute an arbitrary active hard function for the stationary one.

## 2. A positive margin in the penultimate unit-step residual

The interpolation inequality Q_{n,n-1}<=0, together with (1), gives

    f_{n-1}-||p||^2/2 >= f_n+||g||^2/2,
    delta >= q/2+||g||^2/2 > q/2.                          (2)

The strictness holds because q=2f_n>0 implies g_n!=0. If B=prod_t(1+h_t) is the elementary terminal radius bound for normalized initial distance, convexity further gives

    ||g||^2>=q^2/(4B^2),
    delta>=q/2+q^2/(8B^2).                                 (3)

This is a constraint on the actual full stationary primal, including the case q>tau.

## 3. Exact obstruction to certificate inflation followed by final-step blending

Suppose one first changes only the certificate at the SAME h, perhaps increasing its level from q to q', to create a positive new penultimate star-outgoing multiplier nu'. Every such feasible certificate must satisfy, on the old matching legal primal,

    q' >= q+nu' delta.                                     (4)

Indeed its PSD identity gives q'>=2f_n+nu' delta after the other nonnegative interpolation contributions are dropped.

The largest permitted final-step convex blend then certifies the value 2q'/(2+nu'). But (2) and (4) imply

    2q'/(2+nu')
       >= q + nu'||g_n||^2/(2+nu') > q.                    (5)

A smaller blend parameter gives no better certified level. Therefore the two-stage procedure

    raise or alter the certificate at fixed h to create nu'>0,
    then use the proved final-step convex-blend bound,

cannot prove a descent from a full stationary tuple. This is an exact finite inequality, not only a first-order obstruction, and it applies regardless of q-tau.

The original penultimate-flow descent still detects genuinely nonoptimal data, and the transport operation still preserves full feasibility. Equation (5) explains why those operations cannot be bootstrapped into a generic q>tau contradiction after full last-coordinate stationarity has already been reached.

## 4. Implication for the next mechanism

The surviving problem necessarily involves an earlier stepsize change, a nonlinear suffix response, or a quantitative global consequence of the full matrix beyond terminal coordinate optimality. The exact suffix counterexample in research/max2_earlier_reset_obstruction.md forbids carrying final-step convexity backward without additional structure.

The current terminal operations are complete useful constraints, but they do not prove Huber tightness of globally optimal schedules. Further work should not keep rediscovering last-coordinate descent under different notation.

author: max

evidence:
Two exact scope limitations of the current high-dimensional relay models. Both are complete elementary calculations, not verified facts and not obstructions to the unrestricted target.

(1) Pairwise dominance is equivalent to the full residual-sign condition in the Markov-gradient model. Let r_j in(-1,0), D_j>0, C_(j,l)=product_(v=j)^(l-1)r_v, C_(j,j)=1. The residual formula is <Z_i,zeta_j>=-S_(j,i), S_(j,i)=sum_(l=j)^(i-1)D_l C_(j,l). Requiring <Z_i,zeta_j><=0 for every j<i is exactly requiring every S_(j,i)>=0. Taking i=j+2 forces D_j-|r_j|D_(j+1)>=0. Conversely those inequalities imply every S>=0 by pairing terms l=j,j+1, then j+2,j+3, with a positive final singleton if needed. Thus analyzing exact signed sums cannot weaken the adjacent-pair test WHILE retaining this universal nonpositive-residual requirement. A genuinely broader candidate must instead permit S_(j,i)<0 and check the actual affine-plane deficit against the current margin and offsets. For the displayed Moreau model, the exact past-plane comparison is
d alpha_i(alpha_i-C_ij alpha_j)+alpha_j S_(j,i)-eta_i+eta_j>=0,
at both endpoint d=t_i-1 and d=t_i-s_i-1. This retains the signed residual instead of dropping it. Future-plane comparisons use S=0. These endpoint conditions are exact because all comparisons are affine in the partial step sum.

(2) Equal-radius, constant-gradient blocks cannot even start on max3's recursive hostile family, regardless of positive offsets or a closest-minimizer renormalization. Suppose a legal block starts at u and, with a constant nonzero gradient w throughout ordinary sum s and checkpoint b, reaches v=u-(s+b)w. Assume ||u||=||v|| and 0 is a minimizer. At the checkpoint query x=u-sw, smooth-convex cocoercivity against0 gives <w,x>>=||w||^2. Equal endpoint norms imply <w,u>=(s+b)||w||^2/2. Therefore b>=s+2. In the max-affine model this also follows directly from its zero-plane requirement: its active-plane value at x-w is[(s+b)/2-s-1]||w||^2-eta>=0, with eta>=0. Thus no generic interpolation result is needed for the relay obstruction.

Here is a short derivation of the cocoercive inequality, if the broader legal-block statement is used. The descent estimate from x to x-w gives f(x)-min f>=||w||^2/2. Apply the same descent estimate to the convex function q(y)=f(y)-<w,y>, which is minimized at x, starting from0 where its gradient is-w. Then q(x)<=q(w)<=f(0)-||w||^2/2. Combining yields <w,x>>=||w||^2. The descent estimate itself follows by integrating the1-Lipschitz gradient along the segment.

Define H_0 empty and H_(r+1)=(H_r,b_r,H_r), with c=13/5, a=c^(-17), b_r=a c^r. Its sum is S_r=a(c^r-2^r)/(c-2). Immediately before every occurrence of b_r in any H_m lies a full copy of H_r, so the complete prefix sum P is at least S_r. For all r>=0,
S_r+2-b_r=2+a[(3-c)c^r-2^r]/(c-2)>0.
For r>=4 the bracket is nonnegative because (c/2)^r>=(13/10)^4>5/2=1/(3-c). For0<=r<=3 the expression is at least2-(40/3)a>0, since a<c^(-2)=25/169<3/20. Hence every possible first checkpoint obeys b_r<P+2. No partition of this schedule admits the first nonzero equal-radius constant-gradient relay block. This applies to both the independent-state and unit Markov-state models. It does NOT apply to the newer Markov-gradient construction, whose block-start radii change, or to models with varying gradients inside an ordinary block. The true W(H_m) is already large by max3's separate coupled-coordinate candidate; no small-error conclusion is drawn.

author: max
claim: The large arc activation budget survives coordinate rotations: if a checkpoint proximal point is a global minimizer, the next cell's single endpoint plane already forces rho<=1/[epsilon+P+(1+Q)/epsilon]. An aligned-frame attempt fails at an adjacent future plane.
evidence:
Exact local bottleneck in minimum-reset arc relays. Let one two-dimensional future cell start at a prescribed point p+D a, where p is a GLOBAL minimizer of the final one-envelope function, D>0, and a,b are orthonormal input/output axes. Its intended arc data have initial unscaled state r_0=(epsilon+P,-1-Q) and endpoint normal(epsilon,-1). Scaling by D rho and centering at
z_circ=p+D[1-rho(epsilon+P)]a+D rho(1+Q)b
makes the cell start at p+D a. Suppose its nonsmooth local piece is the nonnegative support maximum
Phi(z)=D rho max_(v in V)<v_a a+v_b b,z-z_circ>,
where V includes0 and(epsilon,-1). A maximum of such pieces can vanish at p only if THIS endpoint plane is nonpositive there. Its value before the positive D rho factor is
D[-epsilon+rho epsilon(epsilon+P)+rho(1+Q)].
Thus necessarily
rho <= 1/[epsilon+P+(1+Q)/epsilon].
This is precisely the large A^arc budget in b70f11135ec8688e. It is invariant under rotating a,b or embedding in higher dimension. Passing from the origin to the true closest minimizer cancels this scale only at the first cell; it does not remove the subsequent requirement that an already visited proximal point be a minimizer.

Concrete failed mutation: align the next incoming axis with minus the preceding endpoint gradient and choose rho=1/(epsilon+P), so each center would advance only in a fresh orthogonal direction. At the preceding minimum point p, the new endpoint plane then has strictly positive value D^2 rho^2(1+Q)>0. Consequently the preceding proximal point ceases to be globally minimizing and its prescribed gradient is no longer certified. This is an ADJACENT future-plane failure, independent of all remote Markov comparisons. Adding rotations alone does not repair it.

To avoid this specific bottleneck, a new model must change at least one hypothesis: the checkpoint's proximal value may be positive (carry genuine function-value levels), the local support geometry may change, or the endpoint normal may change. Replacing the required reciprocal-scale bound by an unproved covariance choice would hide the same missing condition. No claim is made that positive-value constructions are impossible or that this obstructs the unrestricted target.

links.next_mechanism: carry positive checkpoint proximal values, not repeated minimizer resets

glossary.A^arc: The exact activation budget epsilon+P+(1+Q)/epsilon for one arc cell.
glossary.P: Horizontal arc displacement in this local calculation.
glossary.Q: Vertical arc displacement in this local calculation.
glossary.a,b: Orthonormal coordinate axes of the one future cell; b here is a vector, not a checkpoint stepsize.

author: max3
claim: C37 closes the fixed-cone/relaxed-projection alternative: every f=mu dist(.,K)^2/2, arbitrary closed convex K and 0<mu<=1, has true-distance normalized error <=mu product(1-mu h_i)^2, attained by a scalar quadratic. Arbitrarily many correlated active-face changes do not help. A bounded cone truncation needs an ACTUALLY active radial cap to escape.
evidence:
# C37. All squared-distance and unsaturated cone-projection witnesses are quadratic-bounded

Status: UNVERIFIED elementary joint candidate. This is a witness-class bound,
not an upper bound on unrestricted W. No external theorem is used as a black box.

Let K be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean
space and 0<mu<=1. Put f(x)=mu dist(x,K)^2/2. The Euclidean projection
p=P_K(x) exists uniquely. Its variational inequalities imply that
x-P_K(x) is firmly nonexpansive; taking differences of the two minimizing
distance expressions shows grad f(x)=mu(x-P_K(x)). Consequently f is convex,
differentiable and mu-smooth, and argmin f=K.

For any actual GD step with nonnegative physical stepsize h,

    x_next=p+(1-mu h)(x-p).

Using this SAME old point p as a candidate in the next distance minimization,

    dist(x_next,K)<=|1-mu h| dist(x,K).

Iterating gives the exact class-wide bound

    2f(x_n)/dist(x_0,K)^2
        <=mu product_(i<n)(1-mu h_i)^2.                    (1)

The right side is attained by the one-dimensional quadratic
f(x)=mu x^2/2, K={0}. Thus allowing arbitrary dimension, arbitrary curved
convex K, and arbitrarily many changes of active projection face NEVER
improves the quadratic worst-case channel for this squared-distance class.
The denominator is the TRUE initial distance, not distance to an arbitrary
chosen minimizer. If x_0 lies in K the trajectory is stationary.

For the near-critical word H_m with
c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c and
H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), (1) at mu=1 is

    product_(i<n)(h_i-1)^2
       =a^(2(2^m-1)) c^(2(2^m-m-1))
       =(1-1/m)^(2(2^m-1)) c^(-2m).                        (2)

It is therefore exponentially small in 2^m/m, with no hidden fixed-parameter
constant. For other mu, (1) is still exactly bounded by the corresponding
full quadratic channel, without needing an asymptotic estimate.

If C is a closed convex cone containing0, the projection function
F_C(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2) equals
dist(x,C^polar)^2/2. Indeed let u=P_C(x), r=x-u. Testing the projection
inequality at0 and2u gives <u,r>=0; testing arbitrary cone elements gives
r in C^polar. Conversely u·(z-r)<=0 for z in C^polar, proving
r=P_(C^polar)(x). Then F_C(x)=||u||^2/2=dist(x,C^polar)^2/2.

The same bound applies to a bounded polytope cut out of C whenever the
actual projection onto the cone remains in the polytope at EVERY queried
point and terminal point. It then has exactly the same projection, value
and trajectory, and its minimizer set has at least the same old polar
minimizer, so the denominator convention must be checked if it is smaller.
For the standard truncation retaining all extreme rays of a polyhedral cone
at positive lengths, the polar and true initial distance are unchanged, so
(1) applies verbatim.

Accordingly a bounded projection polytope can escape this obstruction only
when its finite radial/face bounds alter at least one relevant projection.
Merely using a narrow wedge or many cone faces, with all radial caps inactive,
does not create a new correlated lower-bound mechanism.

glossary.K_dist: Nonempty closed convex minimizer set in the squared-distance construction.
glossary.C_polar: Polar cone, consisting of z with <z,c><=0 for every c in C.
glossary.mu_dist: Scalar curvature in(0,1] multiplying the squared-distance function.

## 7. The remaining transverse-residual restriction

Nonminimum residuals by themselves do not remove every cause of the
previous exponential loss. Suppose an arbitrary continuation retains
(1), has all new query residuals in E-perpendicular, and prepends k
copies of any fixed c in(1,2). No fresh-orthogonality or specified
conjugate height assumption is made in this paragraph. Its backward
update x_(i-1)=x_i-c g_i and x_i-g_i in E-perpendicular imply

    (x_i)_E=(g_i)_E=-(g_(i-1))_E/(c-1).

Starting from p0, the initial E-component is(-1)^k p0/(c-1)^k.
By minimum rigidity(4), the true squared radius is at least
13/(c-1)^(2k). The retained terminal numerator is3, so the entire
stated transverse-residual class has payoff at most
3(c-1)^(2k)/13. Its ratio to the same-word Huber value
1/(2kc+11) and to1/B_(k+3) tends to0. For the latter use the
accepted polynomial bound B_(k+3)<=1+4(k+3)^p. A polynomial times
(c-1)^(2k) tends to0, since its successive ratio tends to(c-1)^2<1.

This is a scoped obstruction, not an assertion of feasibility for
arbitrary continuation parameters. The explicit repeated law above
still has this planar residual restriction. To leave it, a residual
must have a nonzero E-component. The next result permits exactly
that change and still excludes fixed-triangle recovery on long
prefixes bounded away from2, although with a polynomial cost.

## 8. All-interpolant stable-prefix obstruction

Fix delta in(0,1]. Let any physical prefix r_0,...,r_(k-1) have
0<=r_i<=2-delta, and set S=sum_i r_i. Consider EVERY convex1-smooth
function in EVERY finite dimension whose trajectory on this prefix
ends at the first jet(p0,p0,13/2) of(1) and then realizes ALL of(1).
Earlier gradients, values, residuals and their dependence are arbitrary;
the minimum set may change. For its true initial radius R0,

    R0^2>=13[1+delta S
                   +(delta^2/2)(S^2+sum_i r_i^2)].     (35)

Here R0 is a distance, not the alternate performance normalization.
This result is stronger in domain than the prior[0,1] prefix guard:
it includes any fixed interval of steps strictly below2. It is a
new proof, not an invocation of that unverified guard.

Proof. Minimum rigidity gives min F=F(0)=0 and every minimum z
perpendicular to E. Along the prefix write x_i,g_i,f_i for the actual
jets, with x_k=g_k=p0 and f_k=13/2. Smooth descent gives

    f_i-f_(i+1)>=r_i(1-r_i/2)||g_i||^2.               (36)

Gradient norms do not increase for a physical step r_i in[0,2]. For
r_i>0, adding the two interpolation rows between consecutive jets
gives r_i<g_i-g_(i+1),g_i>>=||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2. Therefore
||g_i||^2-||g_(i+1)||^2
 >=(2/r_i-1)||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2>=0. For r_i=0 the points and gradients
coincide. Hence every preceding ||g_i||^2>=13, and(36) implies

    f_i>=13/2+(13delta/2)sum_(j=i)^(k-1) r_j.         (37)

Fix a closest minimizer z to x_0 and put

    gamma=2(1-delta)/delta,
    P_i=||x_i-z||^2+gamma f_i.

The minimum interpolation row is
<g_i,x_i-z>>=f_i+||g_i||^2/2. Combining it with(36) and the exact
distance update gives

    P_i-P_(i+1)
      >=2r_i f_i+
        r_i[(1-r_i)+gamma(1-r_i/2)]||g_i||^2
      =2r_i f_i+[r_i(2-delta-r_i)/delta]||g_i||^2
      >=2r_i f_i.                                    (38)

Smoothness from a minimum gives f_0<=R0^2/2, so P_0<=R0^2/delta.
Perpendicularity gives ||p0-z||^2>=13, so P_k>=13/delta. Summing
(38) and using(37) yields

    R0^2/delta>=13/delta+13S
                     +13delta sum_(i<=j) r_i r_j.

Finally sum_(i<=j)r_i r_j=(S^2+sum_i r_i^2)/2. This is(35).
Every zero step and every physical holding step remains in this sum.
No restriction on old-new covariance, rank or conjugate representation
has entered the argument.

### 8.1 Actual mixed words and complete reference comparison

Take m>=1, u in[0,1], and c in(1,3/2], and use the actual word

    h_st=((u,c)^m,2,2,1), n=2m+3,

Using delta=1/2 and dropping the nonnegative sum of squares in(35),

The complete ray reference equals K and equals the Huber value

    F_ray_n(h_st)=K_n(h_st)=1/(2S+11).                 (41)

For multiple checkpoints, every multiplier b_j-1 is at most1, so
successive feasible magnitudes do not increase and z<=m_previous,

There is a complete-reference comparison also for the FULL complex
channel, in the opposite direction from Section4. Choose the actual
real curvature theta=1/[2(S+5)]. It belongs to D_(h_st), and each
factor1-theta h_i is in[0,1]. By induction, a product of such factors
is at least1 minus the sum of their deficits; hence the full terminal
product is at least1/2. The legal scalar quadratic therefore has

    sup_(z in D_(h_st))Gap_(h_st)(z)
      >=theta product_i(1-theta h_i)^2
      >=1/[8(S+5)].                                   (42)

For S>=16, the right side is strictly larger than(40): after clearing
denominators the difference is13S^2-140S-856, positive at16 since

For the ORIGINAL benchmark, accepted b98bb807d514e80d gives

      <=24[1+4(2m+3)^p]/(13m^2) ->0, p=log_2(3)<2.    (43)

This includes the genuine unit step when u=1 and a zero step when

### 8.2 A legal nonminimum calibration on every word(39)

To distinguish failure from nonexistence, use the accepted static
triangle function F_ft from62a7d9329121fd75 itself. For each remaining
prefix mass T>=0, use the point(1+T)p0, gradient p0 and value
13(T+1/2). Its residual T p0 is nonminimum whenever T>0. Indeed
<p0,q0-p0>=-21 and <p0,e0-p0>=-12, so T p0 is a supporting normal
to the triangle at p0. The original projection formula gives this

Its beta is0. All new/new rows are0. New-to-old rows in order(1)
are(0,-6,0,0); old-to-new rows are(0,-21T,-12T,-12T). The new-to-
minimum row is0 and its reverse is-13T. All old rows remain(3).

### 8.3 A necessary quantity for a redesigned suffix

The same proof gives a concrete outgoing interface without retaining
the triangle. Normalize any legal instance to minimum value0. Suppose
the prefix steps are in[0,2-delta], with total S>0, and its last gradient
has squared norm G>0. Let T_end denote the objective value after any
specified subsequent suffix. The norm argument and(36) give

    2T_end/R0^2<=4T_end/[delta^2 G(S^2+sum_i r_i^2)].  (44)

    T_end/G >=delta^2(S^2+sum_i r_i^2)/[4(2S+11)].     (45)

For fixed delta this required ratio grows linearly with S. If G=0,

This is an exact scoped failure of a proposed THIRD repair, not a third
attained construction and not a general impossibility theorem.

Suppose ANY fixed max-affine function has two DISTINCT slopes q,r with
independently fixed offsets o_q,o_r. Other planes may be present.
Assume actual queries realize: a q-stage ending at proximal point y;
a bridge with excess D>=0; an r-stage of ordinary mass M2-1, ending
at z=y-Dq-M2r; a bridge with excess C>=0; and a RETURNED q-stage
of ordinary mass M3-1, ending at w=z-Cr-M3q. Here M2,M3>=1.
These are actual physical updates, not reset states. Heights at y,z,w
may be arbitrary positive values, and no endpoint is assumed minimal.
The named q-plane and r-plane must actually be active at their respective
queries; representing q as a mixture of unrelated active slopes is outside
this specific fixed-two-plane face policy.

Put s=<q,r>, alpha=||q||^2-s, beta=||r||^2-s, and
ell(u)=<q-r,u>+o_q-o_r. The q/r active-plane conditions demand

    ell(y)>=0,      ell(z)<=0,       ell(w)>=0,
    ell(z)=ell(y)-D*alpha+M2*beta,
    ell(w)=ell(z)+C*beta-M3*alpha.                       (15)

In any nontrivial feasible q-r-q path alpha,beta MUST be positive.
If alpha<=0, then beta>0 because alpha+beta=||q-r||^2>0;
ell(z)>=ell(y)+M2*beta>0 contradicts its r guard. If beta<=0,
alpha>0 and ell(w)<=ell(z)-M3*alpha<0 contradicts its q guard.
Thus the first two guards in(15) give beta/alpha<=D/M2, and the last
two give beta/alpha>=M3/C. If C=0 they directly contradict one another.
Consequently every such fixed-two-plane return NECESSARILY obeys

    D*C >= M2*M3.                                      (16)

Offsets, positive affine heights, minimum-level translations or subsequent
terminal completions cannot repair a violation: they cancel from these
ORIGINAL preterminal active-plane comparisons. Other planes only add
guards. The failure already precedes any smoothness or radius issue.

Apply this to the declared first-occurrence physical prefix

    (H_j,b_j,H_j,b_(j+1),H_(j+1),b_(j+2),
        H_(j+2),b_(j+3)),                               (17)

using ONE enclosing m>=7, j+3<m, and tau=1/4 throughout. Define
lambda=1+sqrt2, beta_h=1-1/(4m), c_h=lambda*(1+1/(4m)),
a_h=beta_h/c_h, H_0=(), H_(l+1)=(H_l,1+a_h*c_h^l,H_l),
S_l=sum H_l, b_l=1+a_h*c_h^l. Induction on the mass identity gives

    1+S_l=v_h*c_h^l+(1-v_h)*2^l,  v_h=a_h/(c_h-2) in(0,1).

Indeed c_h-2>1/lambda>a_h, c_h<3. For the q-r-q assignment in(17),
D=a_h*c_h^(j+1), C=a_h*c_h^(j+2),
M2=1+S_(j+1)>v_h*c_h^(j+1),
M3=1+S_(j+2)>v_h*c_h^(j+2). Therefore

    D*C/(M2*M3)<(a_h/v_h)^2=(c_h-2)^2<1.

This contradicts(16), even with independent affine offsets and POSITIVE
endpoint heights. Thus this specific first-occurrence two-slope-return
repair cannot be instantiated on the actual inherited hierarchy. The
explicit return Law2 is legal because its declared physical data instead
give D*C/(M2*M3)=4. These two statements concern different physical
words; no ratio is silently substituted or reset.

This does not exclude interleaved visits with changing gradients within
a face/edge, more than two returning slopes, nonlinear curved regions,
different physical checkpoint selections, or other full smooth functions.
It does not give an upper bound on W_n(H_m). It is useful because it
identifies a debt unaffected by the newly proposed affine-height freedom.

## 3. Exact physical suffix products and the selected terminal law

Write sbit(L) for the binary digit sum of a nonnegative integer L, including
sbit(0)=0. For 0<=L<=n define the product of the FINAL L actual factors:

    r_L=product_(t=n-L)^(n-1)(h_t-1), r_0=1.

The index j counted backward from the final physical step has
h_(n-j)-1=a*c^v2(2^m-j)=a*c^v2(j), for 1<=j<2^m. The valuation equality
follows by factoring the exact power of2 from j: the remaining difference
from2^m is odd. For any L, sum_(j=1)^L v2(j)=sum_(t>=1)floor(L/2^t).
Writing L in binary and summing each digit's contributions gives
sum_(t>=1)floor(L/2^t)=L-sbit(L). Therefore the EXACT suffix identity is

    r_L=beta^L*c^(-sbit(L)), 0<=L<=n.                 (3.1)

No product or recurrence has been numerically evaluated. In particular
s:=r_n=beta^n/c^m, and the signed full-word product is -s since n is odd.
Define the actual terminal coefficient and its absolute scale by

    k_i=h_i product_(i<t<n)(1-h_t),
    u_i=|k_i|, U=sum_(i<n)u_i, rho_i=u_i/U.

If L=n-1-i, adding the next backward factor shows

    u_i=r_L+r_(L+1), k_i=(-1)^L u_i=(-1)^i u_i.       (3.2)

Thus all u_i are strictly positive. The last three are

    u_z=b, u_(z-1)=a(1+beta), u_(z-2)=b*a*beta,
    u_0=(b/a)s.                                      (3.3)

Expanding a product over the m binary digits gives the finite identity

    Z=sum_(L=0)^n r_L=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1+beta^(2^j)/c),
    U=2Z-1-s <2(3/2)^m.                              (3.4)

The last inequality uses beta<1 and c>2. The three distinct last terms
in (3.3), with (2.1), give

    U>4/3+5/8+7/18=169/72>7/3.                       (3.5)

Both laws use these SAME explicit terminal probabilities:

    alpha_star=p, alpha_i=(1-p)rho_i=delta*u_i,
    delta=(1-p)/U, rplus=1-delta, rminus=1+delta,
    v=k-alpha.                                       (3.6)

They sum to1 and are strictly positive on every original queried sample
and the optimum. They are probabilities on real original rows, not on a
selected child interface. Since U>7/3, one has 0<delta<3/7, rplus>1/2,
and 1<rminus<3/2. Precisely

    v_i=rplus*u_i for i even,
    v_i=-rminus*u_i for i odd.                        (3.7)

Several uniform small-initial-weight bounds will be used. The binomial
expansion implies n=2^m-1>m(m-1)/2>128m for m>=1536. Also
(1-eps)^(-n)>(1+eps)^n>=1+n*eps, so beta^n<1/33. From Aword<c^m,
s/p=beta^n*Aword/c^m<beta^n. Because b/a=1+1/a<4,

    s<p/33, u_0<4p/33<p/8,
    alpha_0<p/8, rho_0<3p/56<1/10.                  (3.8)

These are symbolic inequalities uniform in all enclosing m in the task.

## 4. Full original coordinates and the complete signed matching

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep arbitrary independent
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n, with every original position defined by

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

The residual orientation is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Legal actual jets obey Q_ij<=0. For i<n let y_i=x_i-g_i and
Delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2, with the corresponding star quantities zero.
Let e be the all-ones column of length n, e_i its coordinate columns, and
T=T82 the lower triangular matrix T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, zero for t>i.
For vector columns g=(g_0,...,g_(n-1)) and y=(y_0,...,y_(n-1)),

    y=e*x_0-Tg, g=T^(-1)(e*x_0-y).                    (4.1)

This is invertible on the ENTIRE formal space. Explicitly, if
pi_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t), then

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
          +sum_(j<i)h_j product_(j<t<i)(1-h_t)*y_j.  (4.2)

Substitution into x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i*y_i proves

    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y, e^T k=1+s, T^T k=h.           (4.3)

For the latter identity, h_j=1-(1-h_j) telescopes on each suffix:
k_i+h_i sum_(j>i)k_j=h_i. In particular e^T v=p+s.
The cumulative terminal probabilities, distinct from detail weights below,
are Cprob_i=p+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j. Define

    R_i=h_i*Cprob_i-alpha_i,
    t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j, t=Te,
    Uclock=sum_i R_i=t^T v,
    gamma=2p/(p+s), eta=(p-s)/(p+s).

Then T^T v=R and
R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i>0. Thus Uclock>0,
1<gamma<2, eta>0 and gamma=1+eta. In particular

    R_0=bp+a*alpha_0, H=p+s-v_0=p+alpha_0-s/a,
    bp<R_0<25p/16, 7p/8<H<9p/8.                     (4.4)

The lower bound on H follows from H=p+s-rplus*u_0>p-u_0; its upper
bound follows from the second expression in (4.4).
The actual terminal center is V=-s*x_0+v^T y.

For the moment let w_i>0 be arbitrary DETAIL weights, Ww=sum_i w_i,
and let d be any real column with e^T d=0. Define

    K=diag(w)-w*w^T/Ww,
    A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww+B, B^T=-B, Be=0,
    P=K+gamma*v*v^T, N=T^T(P+A).                     (4.5)

Thus Ke=0, A^T=-A and Ae=d. The matrices are instantiated explicitly in
Sections6 and7; an arbitrary sign-feasible B is NOT a proposed result.
Every scalar entry is

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                                      +gamma*R_i*v_j. (4.6)

The entire ORIGINAL SIGNED coefficient array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,n-1},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for i!=j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i=2p*R_i+(T^T d)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i
                      =(Kt)_i+gamma*Uclock*v_i-(At)_i-2alpha_i,
    lambda_(i,i)=0.                                  (4.7)

Signs are not presumed. This lists every original coefficient, including
both optimum orientations and the actual outgoing terminal distribution.
For each prefix index i, the outgoing sum is N_ii, while the incoming
PREFIX sum is N_ii-2alpha_i. The incoming terminal coefficient2alpha_i
therefore gives zero total divergence at i. Terminal divergence is2;
optimum divergence is-2. Consequently all original sampled values cancel
in M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.

To check the quadratic directly, Q_ij=Delta_i-Delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>
for prefix indices, including star. The prefix value terms cancel the
-2sum alpha_i Delta_i from the outgoing terminal expansion. The remaining
prefix term is -g^T N y. Since N=T^T(P+A), this equals

    -<x_0,e^T(P+A)y>+y^T P y,
    e^T P=2p*v^T, e^T A=-d^T.

The terminal expansion contributes ||g_n-V||^2-||V||^2. Completing the
common square gives the full identity, on arbitrary original vectors,

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2+y^T K y
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2
       +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,d^T y>.                (4.8)

For an expansion check, the unsquared prefix terms are
(q-s^2)||x_0||^2+2(s-p)<x_0,v^T y>+eta||v^T y||^2
+y^T K y+<x_0,d^T y>. The relation eta(p+s)=p-s proves (4.8).

## 5. Weighted completion, the real common derivative, and a row invariant

Let ybar_w=sum_i w_i*y_i/Ww. Since sum_i d_i=0, expanding the squares gives

    sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
    =y^T K y+<x_0,d^T y>+J||x_0||^2,
    J=(1/4)sum_i d_i^2/w_i.                          (5.1)

Thus the COMPLETE factor is

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
       +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2+(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2.  (5.2)

The charge J is paid ONCE globally. No child gradient, common mode, leaf,
checkpoint, terminal square or initial cross derivative has been removed.
The detail form has kernel exactly the constant y columns, because every
w_i>0. The common square controls that remaining direction since e^T v>0.

Full PSD in (5.2) is EQUIVALENT to q>=p^2+J. To prove necessity take scalar
x_0=1, set c0=1+[sum_i v_i*d_i/(2w_i)]/(p+s), y_i=c0-d_i/(2w_i),
and g_n=p. The weighted mean of y is c0 because sum d_i=0. All detail,
common and terminal squares vanish. Reconstruct each original g_i by
(4.2). The value of M is exactly q-p^2-J. This is a formal full-space
negative direction if that quantity is negative; it is NOT an actual
interpolable primal trajectory.

Setting every original queried gradient equal to an arbitrary vector G
instead gives y_i=x_0-t_iG. Directly in (4.8),

    R_common=(q-p^2)||x_0||^2-(d^T t)<x_0,G>
                      +(t^T Kt+eta*Uclock^2)||G||^2. (5.3)

The genuine nonzero initial/common derivative is -(d^T t)x_0. A balanced
B changes neither this derivative nor the full square polynomial.

Now derive the original FIRST-ROW off-diagonal sum including d_0.
The first column of T is (1,b,...,b)^T. Since K has column sums zero,
(T^T K)_00=-a*K_00. Skewness gives A_00=0, and e^T A=-d^T gives
(T^T A)_00=-b*d_0. Meanwhile (T^T d)_0=-a*d_0. Subtracting the diagonal
from the row sum in (4.7) yields

    sum_(j>0) N_0j
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*(p+s-v_0)+d_0
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H+d_0.                     (5.4)

Every balanced B leaves this sum invariant. Nonnegative finite first-row
multipliers require the right side to be <=0. A balanced correction can
redistribute that sum among entries; it cannot change the sum itself.

There is also an exact inverse-metric price for this invariant. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz on i>0 gives
sum_(i>0)d_i^2/w_i >=d_0^2/(Ww-w_0), since sum_(i>0)d_i=-d_0.
Consequently

    J>=d_0^2/(4*K_00), K_00=w_0(1-w_0/Ww).          (5.5)

Equality holds precisely when d_i=-d_0*w_i/(Ww-w_0) for every i>0.
Because H>0, (5.4)--(5.5) imply for any nonnegative first row

    J>=(a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H)^2/(4*K_00)
      >=a*gamma*R_0*H.                               (5.6)

The final inequality expands the nonnegative square
(a*K_00-gamma*R_0*H)^2. This is a necessary first-row screen, NOT a
sufficient certificate condition. The two selected laws now instantiate
all weights and skew matrices rather than leaving the screen unsolved.

## 6. Law A: exact tail metric with minimum-price distributed imbalance

For EVERY kappa>0 and tau>=0 choose

    w_i=kappa*u_i, Ww=kappa*U,
    d=tau*(rho-e_0),
    A_A=tau*(rho*e_0^T-e_0*rho^T), B_A=0.             (6.1)

Here A_A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww exactly, and A_A e=d. The imbalance is
negative at0 and positive at EVERY other actual queried index, not just
at one endpoint. It attains equality in (5.5). The metric is nonisotropic
because u_0<p/8 whereas u_z=b>4/3. The terminal probabilities remain (3.6).

The exact global charge and common derivative are

    J_A=tau^2*(1-rho_0)/(4*kappa*u_0),
    d^T t=tau*(tbar-1), tbar=sum_i rho_i*t_i.          (6.2)

Thus (5.2) is a fully specified factor iff q>=p^2+J_A.
For a literal scalar description of EVERY finite entry put
F_i=u_i+h_i sum_(j>i)u_j. Then

    N^A_ij=kappa*(u_i*1_(i=j)+h_i*u_j*1_(j>i)-F_i*rho_j)
          +gamma*R_i*v_j
          +tau*((F_i/U)*1_(j=0)-1_(i=0)*rho_j).      (6.3)

Together with (4.7), this is the complete array. Both optimum orientations
can also be written explicitly:

    mu_0=2p*R_0+a*tau*(1-rho_0)>0,
    mu_i=2p*R_i+tau*F_i/U>0 for i>0,
    nu^A_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)+gamma*Uclock*v_i
                         -tau*(rho_i-1_(i=0)*tbar)-2alpha_i. (6.4)

All terminal outgoing signs and all outgoing optimum signs pass. No sign
is silently assigned to nu^A or an off-diagonal -N^A.

### 6.1 A first-row charge obstruction at the assigned target

Since v_z=rplus*u_z, the actual first-to-last queried entry is

                                +gamma*R_0*rplus*u_z. (6.5)

If lambda_(0,z)=-N^A_0z>=0, positivity of rho_z gives

Apply (a*x+C)^2/(4x)>=a*C for x=kappa*u_0>0 and

The strict lower bounds use a*b>4/9, gamma>1, R_0>bp, U>7/3 and

## 7. Law B: an explicit balanced transport that repairs the entire first row

Keep the SAME w,d,alpha,p and arbitrary kappa>0,tau>=0 as in Law A.
Define the probability column on noninitial queried samples

    r_0^pool=0, r_i^pool=u_i/(U-u_0) for i>0,
    chi=e_0-r^pool,
    xi=gamma*R_0/a,
    bvec_0=0, bvec_i=xi*(v_i-H*r_i^pool) for i>0,
    B_B=chi*bvec^T-bvec*chi^T,
    A_B=A_A+B_B.                                     (7.1)

The r^pool column is distinct from the suffix product r_L. Its denominator
is positive, and its entries sum to1. Since sum_(i>0)v_i=H, both chi and
bvec have sum zero. Therefore B_B is skew AND B_B e=0. In particular
A_B e=d, and the entire factor (5.2), charge (6.2), and real derivative
(5.3) are unchanged. There is no hidden skew unknown in this law.

For complete scalar coefficients define
C_i=chi_i+h_i sum_(j>i)chi_j and
E_i=bvec_i+h_i sum_(j>i)bvec_j. Then

    N^B_ij=N^A_ij+C_i*bvec_j-E_i*chi_j.              (7.2)

Equations (4.7), (6.3), (7.1)--(7.2) specify EVERY original coefficient.
The outgoing optimum coefficients are still the strictly positive mu_i
in (6.4). The incoming optimum coefficients are

    nu^B_i=nu^A_i-chi_i*(bvec^T t)+bvec_i*(chi^T t).  (7.3)

No positivity of these incoming coefficients is assumed.

### 7.1 The entire first row is explicitly equalized

For j>0, B_B,0j=bvec_j. Because B_B has zero column sums,
(T^T B_B)_0j=-a*bvec_j. Substituting (7.1) in (6.3) yields

    N^B_0j=r_j^pool*S0,
    S0=(a*kappa*u_0-tau)*(1-rho_0)+gamma*R_0*H.      (7.4)

In particular ALL original finite first-row multipliers are nonnegative

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).           (7.5)

This realizes the invariant (5.4), rather than assuming it can be repaired.
It changes the demanding Law A quantity U-1+p in (6.6) to the much smaller
H/(1-rho_0). Thus the Law A charge obstruction does NOT transfer to Law B.

The simultaneous first-row and full-PSD conditions at qtar are nonvacuous.
Within this same two-parameter law choose the explicit member

    kappa_0=gamma*R_0*H/[a*u_0*(1-rho_0)],
    tau_0=2*gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).                    (7.6)

These are positive. Equation (7.4) gives N^B_0j=0 for every j>0, and

Consequently p^2+J_A<3p^2<p/2<qtar, because p<1/128 and

full factor at the target with all finite first-row multipliers zero,

It remains a FAILED certificate because the complete array still has a

## 2. Problem, accepted interfaces, and physical word

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n and smoothness L>0,
W_n(h) is the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite Euclidean
dimension, convex differentiable L-smooth f with an attained minimizer,
and x_0!=x_star, under x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R.
The original question is whether W_n_star/U_n^ZJ tends to1, where
W_n_star=inf_(h>=0)W_n(h), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, and the original all-split
benchmark has

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt(x^2+6xy+y^2))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)).

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the signed residual orientation and
full terminal-square certificate interpretation. Only incoming edges
at the ACTUAL unqueried terminal may be deleted; no queried-prefix
coordinate or constraint is removed. Accepted931b9653ce0f7201 supplies

The accepted residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

For i<n set y_i=x_i-g_i and delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2. Then

    y=e*x_0-Ltri*g,
    g=Ltri^(-1)(e*x_0-y),
    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y.                                (4.1)

Ltri is invertible with diagonal1. More explicitly, with
pi_i=product_(j<i)(1-h_j),

             +sum_(j<i)h_j product_(j<j'<i)(1-h_j')y_j.

The actual terminal gradient remains independently free.

Choose any z with e^T z=E, positive weights w_i, and zero-sum zeta.
Let Ww=sum_i w_i and define

    K=diag(w)-ww^T/Ww,
    P=K+vv^T+eta zz^T,
    d=zeta+F(v-z),
    A^T=-A, Ae=d, N=Ltri^T(P+A).                     (4.2)

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,l},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for distinct i,j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i.           (4.3)

Diagonal multipliers vanish. In scalar entries,

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(r'>i)(K_(r',j)+A_(r',j))
                          +R_i v_j+eta Zout_i z_j,
    Zout=Ltri^T z.                                  (4.4)

an existence assertion. The finite prefix outgoing total at i is N_ii,

and optimum divergence-2. All sampled values cancel in

## 5. General optimum moments, complete first-row moments, literal skew

From Pe+d=2p v+zeta, the outgoing optimum vector is

    mu=2pR+Ltri^T zeta.                              (5.1)

The incoming vector is

    nu=Kt+Vv+eta Zz-At-2alpha.                       (5.2)

Since e^T A=-d^T and t^T At=0, its EXACT moments are

    M0=e^T nu=2pV+theta-2(1-p),
    M1=t^T nu=X+V^2+eta Z^2-2alpha^T t.              (5.3)

A nonnegative nu necessarily has M0>=0 and M0<=M1<=T M0.
Conversely the isolated two-moment problem has the nonnegative endpoint
solution

    nu_target=((T M0-M1)/Delta)e_0
                          +((M1-M0)/Delta)e_l.      (5.4)

This is not sufficient for the finite multiplier signs.
For ANY specified compatible nu_target let

    rvec=Kt+Vv+eta Zz-2alpha-nu_target,
    tmean=(e^T t)/n, cvec=t-tmean*e, Ve=cvec^T cvec>0,
    A0=(d e^T-e d^T)/n,
    fvec=rvec-tmean*d+(d^T t)e/n,
    A=A0+(fvec cvec^T-cvec fvec^T)/Ve.               (5.5)

The two moment identities imply e^T rvec=-d^T t and t^T rvec=0.
Thus e^T fvec=0 and cvec^T fvec=0. Multiplication shows Ae=d and

Every other completion is A+C with C^T=-C and Ce=Ct=0.
Such C leaves the polynomial, mu,nu and all moment tests below unchanged.

For the first row define

    S0=sum_(j>0)N_0j,
    P0=sum_(j>0)(t_j-1)N_0j,
    G0=P0-Delta*S0=sum_(j>0)(t_j-T)N_0j.

The first row of Ltri^T is b e^T-a e_0^T. Write
